title: 1 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 9.

questions.question: What two buildings had Solomon finished building when the LORD appeared to him the second time?
options: The house of the LORD and the king's house
The house of the LORD and the temple of Baal
The king's house and the palace of Pharaoh
The city walls and the king's house
questions.correctAnswer: The house of the LORD and the king's house
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:1 states Solomon had finished the building of the house of the LORD and the king's house.

questions.question: Where had the LORD appeared to Solomon the first time before this second appearance?
questions.correctAnswer: At Gibeon
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:2 mentions the LORD appeared to Solomon the second time as he had at Gibeon.

questions.question: According to the LORD, what did He do to the house Solomon built?
options: Hallowed it to put His name there forever
Made it a place for sacrifices to Baal
questions.correctAnswer: Hallowed it to put His name there forever
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:3 states the LORD said He had hallowed the house Solomon built to put His name there forever.

questions.question: What condition did the LORD give Solomon for establishing his throne forever?
options: Walking before Him in integrity and keeping His statutes
questions.correctAnswer: Walking before Him in integrity and keeping His statutes
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:4 explains the LORD's condition that Solomon walk before Him in integrity and keep His statutes.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise about the throne of Solomon's kingdom if he obeyed?
options: It would be established forever upon Israel
It would be taken away immediately
It would be shared with other kings
It would be temporary and short-lived
questions.correctAnswer: It would be established forever upon Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:5 states the LORD promised to establish Solomon's throne forever upon Israel if he obeyed.

questions.question: What would happen if Solomon or his children turned away from following the LORD?
options: Israel would be cut off from the land the LORD gave them
The LORD would bless them with more cities
questions.correctAnswer: Israel would be cut off from the land the LORD gave them
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:6-7 says if Solomon or his children turned away, Israel would be cut off and the house cast out of the LORD’s sight.

questions.question: What would people say when they passed by the high house built by Solomon if Israel turned from God?
options: "Why hath the LORD done thus unto this land, and to this house?"
"Praise be to the LORD for this house"
"This is the greatest house in all the lands"
questions.correctAnswer: "Why hath the LORD done thus unto this land, and to this house?"
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:8 says passersby would be astonished and ask why the LORD did this to the land and house.

questions.question: Why would the LORD bring evil upon Israel according to the answer people would give?
options: Because they forsook the LORD and worshipped other gods
Because they built the house too quickly
Because they did not build enough cities
Because they did not pay enough tribute
questions.correctAnswer: Because they forsook the LORD and worshipped other gods
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:9 explains the evil came because Israel forsook the LORD and served other gods.

questions.question: How many years did it take Solomon to build the house of the LORD and the king's house?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty years
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:10 states it took Solomon twenty years to build both houses.

questions.question: What did Solomon give to Hiram king of Tyre in exchange for cedar and gold?
options: Twenty cities in the land of Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty cities in the land of Galilee
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:11 records Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in Galilee.

questions.question: True or False: Hiram was pleased with the cities Solomon gave him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:12 states Hiram came to see the cities and they pleased him not.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD said His eyes and heart would be in the house Solomon built perpetually.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:3 says the LORD's eyes and heart shall be there perpetually in the house Solomon built.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon made the children of Israel to be bondmen for the work.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:22 clarifies Solomon did not make the children of Israel bondmen but rather officers and warriors.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year on the altar he built.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:25 records Solomon offered burnt and peace offerings three times yearly on the altar.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 9, which event comes first?
options: The LORD appears to Solomon the second time
Hiram visits the cities Solomon gave him
Solomon makes a navy of ships
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD appears to Solomon the second time
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:2 describes the LORD's second appearance to Solomon, which occurs before the other events later in the chapter.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did King Solomon give to Hiram in exchange for cedar trees, fir trees, and gold?
options: Twenty cities in the land of Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty cities in the land of Galilee
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:11 states that Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee after Hiram had furnished Solomon with cedar, fir, and gold.

questions.question: How did Hiram feel about the cities Solomon gave him?
options: He offered to trade them back
questions.correctAnswer: They pleased him not
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 9:12, Hiram came to see the cities and they did not please him.

questions.question: What name did Hiram give to the cities Solomon gave him?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of Cabul
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:13 records that Hiram called the cities 'the land of Cabul' to this day.

questions.question: How much gold did Hiram send to King Solomon as recorded in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Sixscore talents
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:14 mentions that Hiram sent sixscore (120) talents of gold to Solomon.

questions.question: What was the reason for the levy raised by King Solomon?
options: To build the house of the LORD, his own house, Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and several cities
To fund a war against Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: To build the house of the LORD, his own house, Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and several cities
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:15 explains that the levy was raised to build the temple, Solomon's house, Millo, Jerusalem's wall, and cities like Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

questions.question: How did Pharaoh king of Egypt contribute to Solomon's possession of Gezer?
options: He took Gezer, burnt it, slew its inhabitants, and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife
He gifted it to Solomon without conditions
He purchased it from the Canaanites
He conquered it for Solomon during battle
questions.correctAnswer: He took Gezer, burnt it, slew its inhabitants, and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:16 says Pharaoh took Gezer by force, destroyed it, and gave it as a present to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

questions.question: Which cities did Solomon build or rebuild according to the chapter?
options: Gezer, Bethhoron the nether, Baalath, and Tadmor
questions.correctAnswer: Gezer, Bethhoron the nether, Baalath, and Tadmor
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:17-18 lists these cities as ones Solomon built or rebuilt.

questions.question: What types of cities did Solomon have throughout his dominion?
options: Cities of store, cities for chariots, and cities for horsemen
questions.correctAnswer: Cities of store, cities for chariots, and cities for horsemen
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:19 explains Solomon had cities for storage, chariots, and horsemen, in addition to his other building desires.

questions.question: What did Solomon do with the remaining people of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites?
questions.correctAnswer: Levy them to bondservice
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:20-21 reveals Solomon imposed a tribute of forced labor on these remaining peoples whom Israel could not utterly destroy.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon made the children of Israel bondmen for his works.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:22 clearly states Solomon did not make the children of Israel bondmen but rather used them as warriors, servants, princes, and captains.

questions.question: How many chief officers did Solomon appoint over the workers?
questions.correctAnswer: Five hundred and fifty
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:23 mentions that Solomon appointed 550 chief officers to oversee the laborers.

questions.question: What did Solomon build for Pharaoh's daughter?
options: A house in the city of David
questions.correctAnswer: A house in the city of David
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:24 states Pharaoh's daughter went from the city of David to her house that Solomon built for her.

questions.question: How often did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar he built unto the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times in a year
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:25 records that Solomon offered these offerings three times annually and burnt incense on the altar before the LORD.

questions.question: Where did Solomon establish a navy of ships?
options: Eziongeber, beside Eloth, on the Red Sea shore in Edom
questions.correctAnswer: Eziongeber, beside Eloth, on the Red Sea shore in Edom
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:26 explains Solomon made a navy of ships at Eziongeber near Eloth on the Red Sea in Edom.

questions.question: What was the result of Hiram sending shipmen with Solomon’s servants?
options: They brought back 420 talents of gold from Ophir
They established a trade route to Egypt
They brought back cedar and fir trees
questions.correctAnswer: They brought back 420 talents of gold from Ophir
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:27-28 states that Hiram sent experienced shipmen with Solomon's men who fetched 420 talents of gold from Ophir.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice upon, according to 1 Kings 9:21?
options: The leftover children of Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.correctAnswer: The leftover children of Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:20-21 explains that Solomon imposed a tribute of bondservice on the remaining children of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not destroyed by Israel.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 9:22, what role did Solomon assign to the children of Israel?
options: Men of war, servants, princes, captains, and rulers
questions.correctAnswer: Men of war, servants, princes, captains, and rulers
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states that Solomon did not make the children of Israel bondmen but made them men of war and his servants and rulers in various military and administrative capacities.

questions.question: How many chief officers were over Solomon's work, according to 1 Kings 9:23?
questions.explanation: Verse 23 specifies that there were 550 chief officers who bore rule over the people working for Solomon.

questions.question: Who came up out of the city of David to her house built by Solomon, as mentioned in 1 Kings 9:24?
questions.correctAnswer: Pharaoh's daughter
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states that Pharaoh's daughter came up from the city of David to the house Solomon had built for her.

questions.question: How many times a year did Solomon offer burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar he built, according to 1 Kings 9:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: Verse 25 clearly says Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year on the altar he built.

questions.question: Where did Solomon build a navy of ships, as described in 1 Kings 9:26?
options: Eziongeber, beside Eloth on the Red Sea shore
questions.correctAnswer: Eziongeber, beside Eloth on the Red Sea shore
questions.explanation: Verse 26 states Solomon built a navy in Eziongeber beside Eloth, located on the shore of the Red Sea in Edom.

questions.question: Who sent servants skilled in the sea to join Solomon’s navy, according to 1 Kings 9:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Hiram
questions.explanation: Verse 27 reveals that Hiram sent his servants, skilled shipmen, to accompany Solomon’s servants in the navy.

questions.question: From which place did Solomon’s navy bring gold, and how much, according to 1 Kings 9:28?
questions.correctAnswer: Ophir; 420 talents
questions.explanation: Verse 28 reports the navy fetched 420 talents of gold from Ophir and brought it to Solomon.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'bondservice' in the context of 1 Kings 9:21?
options: It refers to forced labor or tribute imposed on non-Israelite inhabitants
It means voluntary service by Israelite citizens
It describes the priestly duties in the temple
It refers to military conscription of Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to forced labor or tribute imposed on non-Israelite inhabitants
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term behind 'bondservice' (עֲבֹדַת סֶ֑רֶךְ) indicates compulsory labor or tribute, here applied to the leftover Canaanite peoples as per 1 Kings 9:21.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of a king's responsibility to walk in integrity before God as stated in 1 Kings 9:4-5?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 17:18-20
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 17:18-20 instructs kings to write and follow the law, walking in God's statutes with integrity, reflecting the promise and conditions in 1 Kings 9:4-5.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the conditional promise and warning spoken by the LORD to Solomon in 1 Kings 9:4-9?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The structure in 1 Kings 9:4-9 uses chiasm, a literary device where ideas are presented and then reversed (promise of blessing if obeyed, warning if disobeyed), emphasizing covenant fidelity.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 9:16-17, which city did Solomon rebuild after Pharaoh of Egypt gave it to his daughter as a dowry?
questions.correctAnswer: Gezer
questions.explanation: Verse 16-17 recount Pharaoh took Gezer, burned it, and gave it as a present to his daughter Solomon’s wife; Solomon rebuilt Gezer afterwards.

questions.question: What is the historical significance of Solomon’s building projects such as Millo and city walls mentioned in 1 Kings 9:15 and 9:24?
options: They fortified Jerusalem and solidified Solomon’s political power
They were purely decorative projects for the temple
They were only administrative centers without military value
They represented foreign architecture imported from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They fortified Jerusalem and solidified Solomon’s political power
questions.explanation: The building of Millo and walls (1 Kings 9:15, 24) served as fortifications and enhanced Solomon’s control over Jerusalem and his kingdom.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 9:22, Solomon made the children of Israel bondmen for labor and tribute.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:22 explicitly states Solomon did not make the children of Israel bondmen but rather men of war and rulers.

questions.question: True or False: The covenantal promise given to Solomon in 1 Kings 9:4-5 foreshadows the eternal kingship of Christ over Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The promise in 1 Kings 9:5 of an everlasting throne on Israel echoes the Messianic hope fulfilled in Christ's eternal reign (cf. Luke 1:32-33).

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What condition does God set for Solomon to establish his throne forever over Israel?
options: Walk before God in integrity of heart and keep His statutes and judgments
Build more cities and fortify Jerusalem
Offer sacrifices three times a year
Maintain a strong navy and trade fleet
questions.correctAnswer: Walk before God in integrity of heart and keep His statutes and judgments
questions.explanation: God promises Solomon that if he walks before Him as David did, in integrity and obedience to His commandments, then his kingdom will be established forever (1 Kings 9:4-5). This shows the conditional nature of God's covenant based on obedience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by God's promise to Solomon that His eyes and heart will be perpetually in the temple Solomon built?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipresence
questions.explanation: God declares His eyes and heart shall be there perpetually (1 Kings 9:3), indicating His omnipresence—being present everywhere, especially in His chosen dwelling place.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 9 depict God’s response to idolatry among Israel and their descendants?
options: God will cut off Israel from the land and cast the temple out of His sight
God will forgive and restore them immediately
God will allow other nations to rule Israel but keep the temple holy
God will send prophets to warn but not punish
questions.correctAnswer: God will cut off Israel from the land and cast the temple out of His sight
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 warn that if Israel turns away to serve other gods, God will remove them from the land and cast away the temple, showing His holiness and justice against sin.

questions.question: What theological significance does the naming of the cities given to Hiram as 'the land of Cabul' have?
options: It signifies displeasure and dissatisfaction with Solomon’s gift
It indicates a covenant of friendship between Solomon and Hiram
It marks the cities as holy and consecrated
It shows Hiram’s acceptance and joy
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies displeasure and dissatisfaction with Solomon’s gift
questions.explanation: Hiram was displeased with the cities given to him and called them 'the land of Cabul' (meaning worthless), indicating the gift did not meet his expectations, reflecting political tensions (1 Kings 9:12-13).

questions.question: What doctrine is exemplified by Solomon making no Israelite a bondman but instead making them warriors, princes, and captains?
options: Doctrine of God's providential care over His covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of God's providential care over His covenant people
questions.explanation: Solomon’s treatment of Israelites as leaders and warriors, not bondservants (1 Kings 9:22), reflects God’s providence in preserving and honoring His covenant community distinct from foreigners subjected to forced labor.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 9 describe the spiritual cause of the calamities that will come upon Israel, according to the explanation given to passersby?
options: Forsaking the LORD and worshipping other gods
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking the LORD and worshipping other gods
questions.explanation: The chapter explicitly states that the reason for the evil upon the land is Israel’s forsaking God and worshipping other gods (1 Kings 9:9), connecting sin directly with judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do 1 Kings 9:5 and 1 Kings 9:6 communicate about God’s covenant with Solomon?
options: God’s covenant blessing is conditional on obedience and disobedience brings judgment
God’s covenant is unconditional and eternal without regard to human actions
God’s covenant is based solely on Solomon’s wisdom
God’s covenant focuses only on material prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant blessing is conditional on obedience and disobedience brings judgment
questions.explanation: Verse 5 promises establishment of the throne if Solomon obeys, while verse 6 warns of judgment if he or his descendants turn away, showing the conditional nature of the covenant.

questions.question: In light of 1 Kings 9, what broader biblical narrative does the building and dedication of the temple represent?
options: God’s desire to dwell among His people and the foreshadowing of Christ as the true temple
The final establishment of earthly kingdoms
A purely political achievement with no spiritual significance
The end of prophecy in Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s desire to dwell among His people and the foreshadowing of Christ as the true temple
questions.explanation: The temple signifies God's presence with Israel (1 Kings 9:3), and biblically it points forward to Christ who embodies God dwelling with humanity (John 1:14).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by His promise to Solomon that His name will be there forever in the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Eternal faithfulness
questions.explanation: God states His name will be there forever (1 Kings 9:3), reflecting His eternal faithfulness to His promises and covenant presence.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 9:26-28 contribute to our understanding of Solomon’s reign in relation to God’s providence and human enterprise?
options: It shows God providentially enabling Solomon’s international trade and naval expansion
It depicts Solomon ignoring God for material gain
It indicates Solomon’s dependence solely on foreign alliances
It emphasizes the futility of human effort without God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God providentially enabling Solomon’s international trade and naval expansion
questions.explanation: The navy and trade missions to Ophir (1 Kings 9:26-28) demonstrate God’s providential blessing on Solomon’s reign, facilitating wealth and influence through human means under divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What theological insight arises from the fact that Solomon levied bondservice on the remaining Canaanite peoples but not on Israelites?
options: God’s covenant people are set apart and not subjected to servitude
God approves of bondage for all peoples
All peoples are equal in roles and servitude
The Israelites were exempt from taxes
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant people are set apart and not subjected to servitude
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 distinguish Israelites from the remaining Canaanites who were subjected to bondservice, illustrating divine election and covenant privilege for Israel.

questions.question: What synthesis about God’s holiness and justice can be drawn from 1 Kings 9:7-9?
options: God’s holiness demands judgment on idolatry, resulting in exile and disgrace
God overlooks idolatry if offerings are made
God punishes only kings, not people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands judgment on idolatry, resulting in exile and disgrace
questions.explanation: These verses show God’s holy presence in the temple and His righteous judgment against idolatry, including exile and becoming a byword among nations.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that ancient Israel’s monarchy was merely political with no divine involvement. What does 1 Kings 9:1-7 teach about God’s active role in Solomon’s reign and the temple?
options: God personally appears to Solomon and sets covenant conditions, showing divine sovereignty over the monarchy
Solomon acted independently without any divine communication
The temple was purely a human political project
God only cared about the sacrifices, not the king
questions.correctAnswer: God personally appears to Solomon and sets covenant conditions, showing divine sovereignty over the monarchy
questions.explanation: The text records God’s second appearance to Solomon and His covenant promises and warnings (1 Kings 9:1-7), affirming divine involvement in Israel’s monarchy and sacred worship.

questions.question: How do 1 Kings 9:10-11 and 1 Kings 9:14 together illustrate the economic and political relationship between Israel and Tyre during Solomon’s reign?
options: Solomon’s building projects were supported by Tyre’s resources, but political tensions remained
Tyre was economically dependent on Israel
There was no cooperation between the two kingdoms
Solomon paid no tribute to Tyre
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon’s building projects were supported by Tyre’s resources, but political tensions remained
questions.explanation: Tyre supplied timber and gold (verses 10-11, 14), yet the gift of cities displeased Hiram, indicating cooperation mixed with political friction.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal lesson do 1 Kings 9:25 and 1 Kings 9:3 convey about true worship and God’s presence?
options: God’s presence is tied to faithful worship and sacrifice as expressions of covenant relationship
Worship is optional and God’s presence is independent
God is indifferent to the temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: God’s presence is tied to faithful worship and sacrifice as expressions of covenant relationship
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states God’s presence in the temple, while verse 25 shows Solomon’s regular offerings, indicating worship is essential to maintain fellowship with God.
